newsitem.title: UK: Britain to offer Hong Kong Asians passports-paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain to offer Hong Kong Asians passports-paper.

text.p: Britain is expected to announce that up to 8,000 mainly Indian and Pakistani citizens of Hong Kong can have full British passports, a British newspaper said on Tuesday.

The Daily Telegraph said the move was a recognition of concerns raised by Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten that non-Chinese ethnic minorities could be rendered stateless when the colony is handed back to China in June.
British Home Secretary Michael Howard could make the announcement as early as Tuesday with a simultaneous announcement expected in Hong Kong.

The move affects those holding passports as British Dependent Territory Citizens who would be eligible for British National Overseas status after the handover but are not also nationals of another country, such as India or Pakistan.
The key test will be whether they are likely to be made stateless after the handover.
The Telegraph quoted British government sources as saying those with dual nationality or the right of abode in another country could not expect British citizenship.
Currently they enjoy only visiting rights to Britain.
Many of the Indians and Pakistanis affected have long ties with Britain dating back to the founding of the colony in the 1840s and have played a prominent role there.
